verses: This is the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way.”
“A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.’”
John the Baptist appeared in the wilderness, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
People went out to him from all of Jerusalem and the countryside of Judea. Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.
John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
And he proclaimed: “After me will come One more powerful than I, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.
I baptize you with water, but He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
As soon as Jesus came up out of the water, He saw the heavens breaking open and the Spirit descending on Him like a dove.
And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.”
At once the Spirit drove Jesus into the wilderness,
and He was there for forty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels ministered to Him.
After the arrest of John, Jesus went into Galilee and proclaimed the gospel of God.
“The time is fulfilled,” He said, “and the kingdom of God is near. Repent and believe in the gospel!”
title: The Beginning
season_line: Today we open Mark, the shortest and fastest of the four Gospels, and it skips Bethlehem entirely to start in the wilderness.
big_idea: The good news begins with God coming near in Jesus, and the right response is to turn toward Him and trust.
frame: Mark doesn't open with advice. He opens with an announcement: God has kept His word and come close. That changes how an ordinary Thursday works. Walking with God doesn't start with getting ourselves in order so He'll show up. It starts with noticing He already has, and then turning our face toward Him. Repentance isn't groveling. It's a turn, and you can make it many times a day. Trust is simply leaning your weight on what God has said. This is the same God who promised a way through the wilderness in {{Isaiah 40:3-5|Isaiah 40:3–5}}, now walking into our story as Jesus. Carry this posture today: turned toward Him, leaning on Him.

carry.text: “The time is fulfilled,” He said, “and the kingdom of God is near. Repent and believe in the gospel!”

glance.head: A promised beginning
glance.line: Mark calls his book good news about Jesus, the Son of God, and ties it to what the prophets promised long ago.

glance.head: John prepares the way
glance.line: John calls people in the wilderness to turn from sin, and he points to Someone far greater coming after him.

glance.head: The Son, loved and tested
glance.line: Jesus is baptized, the Father declares His love, and the Spirit sends Him straight into the wilderness to be tempted.

glance.head: The kingdom is near
glance.line: Jesus begins preaching in Galilee: God's time has come, so turn and trust the good news.

understand: Mark is the shortest Gospel, and it moves fast. Watch for words like 'at once' and immediately. Early church tradition links Mark with Peter, who calls him his son in {{1 Peter 5:13|1 Peter 5:13}}. So we may be hearing Peter's memories, told plainly. Mark's first word, 'beginning,' quietly echoes {{Genesis 1:1|Genesis 1:1}}. God is starting something new.

The quotation in verses 2 and 3 blends {{Malachi 3:1|Malachi 3:1}} with {{Isaiah 40:3|Isaiah 40:3}}. Both promised that God Himself would come, with a messenger going ahead. John's camel hair and leather belt deliberately recall Elijah ({{2 Kings 1:8|2 Kings 1:8}}). Malachi had said an Elijah figure would come before the Lord ({{Malachi 4:5-6|Malachi 4:5–6}}). After about four hundred years of prophetic silence, the voice is back.

At Jesus' baptism, Mark says the heavens were 'breaking open.' That is a strong, tearing word. It answers Isaiah's old cry for God to tear open the heavens and come down ({{Isaiah 64:1|Isaiah 64:1}}). The Father's words echo {{Psalm 2:7|Psalm 2:7}} and {{Isaiah 42:1|Isaiah 42:1}}, naming Jesus as both King and Servant. Then come forty days in the wilderness. They recall Israel's forty years there. Where Israel stumbled, Jesus stands firm for His people.

Verses 14 and 15 sum up everything Jesus will preach. 'The time is fulfilled' means the waiting is over. 'The kingdom of God is near' means God's rule has arrived, in person. The call that follows is simple: repent, meaning turn around, and believe, meaning trust. Mark will spend the rest of his book showing us who this King is.

word.gloss: It means 'good news' or 'glad tidings.' In the Roman world the word was used for royal announcements, like a new king's birth or a victory. Mark uses it for the arrival of the true King.

glow: Prepare the way for the Lord
You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased

god.short: Pray verse 15 slowly and name one specific place you need to turn.
god.full: Read Mark 1:15 aloud and ask God to show you one specific area where you're facing away from Him. Name it plainly, turn it over to Him, and thank Him that the kingdom is near.
god.why: God's promise was that He would come near first ({{Isaiah 40:9-11|Isaiah 40:9–11}}); our turning is a response, not a price.

together.short: Pray one line together: "Lord, we turn toward You and trust You today."
together.full: Before you leave the table, hold hands and pray one sentence together: "Lord, we turn toward You and trust You today."

others.short: Like John, point past yourself: publicly credit a coworker's good work today.
others.full: John gladly made himself smaller so Someone greater could be seen. Today, find a coworker or teammate whose work often goes unnoticed, and name their contribution out loud to others.
others.why: John's joy was in making way for Another ({{John 3:27-30|John 3:27–30}}).

tonight: Where did you sense God near today, and where did you catch yourself facing away from Him?
